blocker.summary: r455 fixed and verified r454's presented_frames diagnostic desync: NativeRuntime::diagnostics() now sums backend_.present_count() and pinned_runtime_->present_count() (additive, never overlapping per the existing pinned_handled_present/use_pinned guards). Relaunched against the real ISO: presented_frames=5 state=2, matching the clean baseline. Also added a capture diagnostic (AC6_NATIVE_CAPTURE=1, new NativeRuntime::readback_offscreen_pixels()/offscreen_error() accessors, no file/PNG output -- just a non-black-pixel and distinct-color count) to verify real visual content, not just an advancing counter. That capture immediately found a SECOND real gap: error=offscreen image is not in a blittable layout. Cross-referenced with r454: on this same run, all 8 real-draw attempts fell back (no pinned shader matched the observed draw state), so PinnedShaderRuntime's edram_rt_valid_ never became true, and publish_write_address's direct present (the VdSwap path, r430/r454) calling execute_frame() with just a PresentPacket does nothing to the image at all when there is no active EDRAM target -- no resolve, and (unlike the old backend_->present_to_offscreen() path, which always cleared) no fallback clear either. This is a real regression versus pre-r454 behavior: every present used to guarantee at least a defined (black) image; now, if no pinned draw ever succeeds in a session, the image stays permanently undefined. Not a crash, presented_frames still correct, but a real step back for anything reading the image itself. Named for r456: guarantee a defined image on the direct-present path even when no pinned draw has ever succeeded, without reintroducing the double-clear/double-present class already fixed once (r432/r454) -- then rerun the capture to verify real visual content. Still not committed -- same reasoning as r454 (entangled with cataloged backlog, and now a second known gap, not just one). Other open items unchanged: reconsider the backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454/r455) once mature; update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (r452/r453, convenience only).
